reviews.rationale: The module sequences one knowledge migration lifecycle; formatting, bootstrap application, and top-level dispatch are extracted, while the remaining effects share ordered plan, approval, rollback, and event contracts.

Move, merge, split, and delete are variants of one exact-approved document-structure command contract and share the same validation, normalization-relocation reporting, materialization event, and rollback boundary.
All functions validate or execute one managed deliberation lifecycle and share the same provider plan, writing contract, checkpoint, and interruption semantics.
The module owns one read-only selection adapter lifecycle; pure projection and authorization, durable record construction, and managed-run composition remain in separate modules.

The module composes one managed provider-run boundary; provider differences remain injected dependencies, while causal validation and assignment finalization are extracted and no unrelated CLI subcommand or persistence policy is owned here.
Inspection, planning, stage application, lint, and receipt formatting all describe one bounded repository-upgrade lifecycle and share a single plan identity.

TLS material loading, dependency and server composition, reload, resource lifecycle orchestration, and health wiring are phases of one Hub deployment boundary; HTTP connection-drain mechanics and domain policy remain in linked modules.

The class owns one external Claude protocol boundary and translates native session, tool, telemetry, stop, and result behavior into common adapter contracts; the accounting declaration remains in a linked descriptor module.

The class owns the Codex provider boundary, selects one injected native transport, and translates thread, turn, telemetry, stop, and result behavior into common adapter contracts; transport parsing and the accounting declaration remain linked modules.

Agent and assignment records, including bounded routine and message-trigger provenance plus recipient acknowledgment, share one project-bound coordination home, validation model, atomic transition and event rollback, and concurrency retry boundary. Pure trigger and admission planning, assignment-DAG cancellation, prepared-completion validation, and workspace lifecycle effects remain in linked modules.
The repository class owns one SQLite persistence boundary for platform bindings, including validation, reads, writes, and transaction-safe state changes.

The module owns one in-memory deliberation state machine; artifact publication failure recording and handoff materialization remain in linked modules, while methods enforce shared history and event invariants.
The allowlists and coordinate validators jointly implement one fail-closed event redaction contract; every branch contributes to the same privacy decision.
The declarative migration catalog and migration runner own one versioned SQLite schema boundary; length is driven by schema history rather than mixed runtime policy.
The store class is one persistence adapter that composes repositories under a shared database, transaction, and schema lifecycle.
Read, lint, query, export, import, and re-export are operations over one external OKF format boundary with shared safety, trust, and byte-preservation rules.

Snapshotting, abort handling, context delivery, turn execution, validation, resource and stage observation composition, and stop are phases of one provider-neutral managed-run state machine; accounting and timing invariants remain in linked modules.

Reservation, completion, recovery projection, target binding, and integrity checks all operate on one immutable rollback replay table and transaction lifecycle; authorization and rollback policy remain outside the adapter.
The class owns one SQLite policy persistence boundary and its approval, verification, transaction, and query operations.

Process control plus Codex and Claude response and usage parsing implement one capability-free provider boundary for typed JSON, semantic compilation, and document normalization contracts; resource admission remains in repository knowledge.
Publication rendering, desired output construction, recorded-output comparison, and plan creation are phases of one deterministic structural compilation contract.

Profiles, envelopes, candidate validation, lifecycle inspection, generation orchestration, candidate storage, planning, and exact-approved apply share one content-bound lifecycle. Observation policy, explicit selection and workset/preflight contracts, shard-cache storage, and CLI parsing or rendering are separate modules.
Plan serialization, safe source inspection, merge planning, lineage updates, and apply are one atomic document-merge responsibility.

Destination safety, plan serialization, lineage, single-output normalization-record preservation, plan creation, and apply are one atomic document-move responsibility; normalization record mechanics remain in a separate bounded module and formatter configuration is outside this transaction.
Heading extraction, destination safety, plan serialization, lineage preservation, and apply are one atomic document-split responsibility.
Journal creation, binding checks, safe writes, rollback, recovery, and cleanup implement one atomic filesystem transaction protocol.
Profile resolution, registry binding, structural refresh, plan creation, and exact-approved apply share one instruction-bridge lifecycle; target construction and classification are extracted.
Query behavior and safe publication access were extracted; the remaining functions exclusively validate manifests, layout, normalization, lineage, and semantic sidecars.
Coordinate extraction, candidate validation, protected-change review, plan creation, and apply implement one byte-safe README improvement contract.
Policy validation, review identity, disposition validation, artifact persistence, and event recording form one exact-review responsibility.
Existing registry inspection, candidate signatures, conflict options, and dispositions jointly produce one read-only reconciliation plan.

Classification, link rebasing, neutral ownership-record migration, machine moves, user updates, serialization, plan creation, and apply are phases of one repository-wide layout transaction; tool-specific formatter configuration is outside this boundary.
Classification, safe reads, source-unit extraction, scan construction, and immutable scan transforms all own the canonical scanned-source aggregate.
Compilation identity, bounded sharding, provider response validation, and candidate assembly are phases of one semantic compiler contract.
Review loading, operation derivation, publication generation, plan creation, and apply share one review-bound materialization contract.
Move, split, and merge lineage creation and validation operate on one lineage schema and safe registry-loading boundary.
Provider configuration merge, runtime integrity, inspection, plan creation, and apply form one fail-closed terminal integration contract.
The module exposes one package-level contract surface for repository scans, plans, operations, lifecycle results, diagnostics, and typed domain failures without owning their implementations.
Current state, continuation import, start, update, and replicated import all preserve one WorkstreamSnapshot aggregate, origin invariant, CAS binding, and durable apply protocol.
Identity calculation, registry validation, service-file inspection, onboarding planning, listing, and registration share one owner-only fleet registry contract.
Source validation, built-in and custom contract construction, conservative composition, listing, resolution, and binding all own one role-contract aggregate.
The file is a declarative schema catalog for one adapter protocol; its length is data-shaped and contains no independent executable workflow.

The module contains only the bounded JSON Schema declarations and inferred payload types for one terminal observation lifecycle; runtime validation, redaction, persistence, and orchestration remain in their owning modules.
The module declaratively registers and exposes validators for the versioned schema catalog; its length follows schema inventory and it owns no domain workflow or external effect.
Case validation, paired timing, quality aggregation, latency statistics, environment capture, and reporting form one reproducible benchmark protocol.
Manifest, SBOM, archive, validation, installation safety, and smoke verification are phases of one Hub distribution artifact contract.
Dependency inventory, manifest, SBOM, archive, platform validation, and verification are phases of one Node distribution artifact contract.
Temporary project setup, process control, HTTPS calls, event observation, assertions, and cleanup compose one end-to-end acceptance scenario; command invocation is a separate thin entrypoint.

Parsing, definition validation, status stabilization, install, compensate, remove, activate, and upgrade operate on one service transaction boundary; status presentation and process exit behavior are isolated in the command adapter.

The module composes the bounded suite, isolated workspaces, provider-neutral evidence selection, paired arm schedule, and cleanup; command invocation, versioned acceptance, report evaluation, provider preparation and transports, and selection policy remain separate.

The module owns one immutable comparison-contract lineage: protocols, schema, suite validation, and pure acceptance evaluation share the same version and gate lifecycle, while provider execution and evidence selection remain separate.

The module declaratively validates one lineage of recent immutable canary checkpoints; preparation, execution, storage, and reporting remain in separate modules, while the length follows explicit version-bound predecessor evidence.

The module composes and validates one lineage of immutable provider-shadow contracts; policy, preparation I/O, execution, observation, and review remain in separate modules, while the length follows explicit historical contract variants.
